title: Blueberry-Balsamic Barbecue Glaze
description: Blueberries, balsamic vinegar and a small spoonful of molasses reduce to a smooth, dark glaze for sauced pork or chicken.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

steps.title: Burst the berries
steps.text: Bring {berries} and {broth} to a gentle simmer in the HexClad. Cover for 5–7 minutes until the berries burst.

steps.title: Build the barbecue base
steps.text: Stir in {vinegar}, {molasses} and {paprika}. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Strain the blueberry base
steps.text: Puree the mixture in the deep jug. Press it through the sieve back into the skillet to catch the skins.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Swirl the warm glaze through thick pork gravy or spoon it over chicken already resting in its braising sauce.

notes: Yield: 1 cup. One serving is 2 tablespoons. Make ahead: Cook and strain the base up to 2 days ahead. Add the slurry when ready to serve. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The blueberry puree freezes well for up to 2 months. Whisk as it warms to restore the glossy texture. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A includes balsamic and smoked paprika. For gentler Option B, replace the vinegar with unsweetened apple juice and omit the paprika. Both versions are dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 21 kcal, 0.4 g protein, 4.7 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 4 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
